speaker: Unknown
en: So, we've been chatting about your famous giveaway, your Legos career advice, this idea of how this advice applies in today's very strange AI world.
zh: 所以，我们一直在聊你那个著名的「送出你的乐高」职业建议，聊这个建议如何应用在当今这个非常奇怪的 AI 世界里。

speaker: Unknown
en: The narrative right now is literally like, okay, we hired this new employee, this new employee is the smartest employee that you have ever met.
zh: 现在的叙事大致就是：好，我们雇了这个新员工，这个新员工是你见过的最聪明的员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want you to pour every single thing that you know into this employee, and then they're going to take your job in six months.
zh: 我要你把你所知道的每一样东西都倾注到这个员工身上，然后六个月后他们就会抢走你的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who the [inaudible 00:00:25] wants to do that?
zh: 谁[听不清 00:00:25]愿意这么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the big question, Molly.
zh: 这是个大问题，Molly。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there any Legos you should not give away?
zh: 有没有哪些乐高是你不应该送出去的？

speaker: Unknown
en: In AI land, I think we got to caveat this.
zh: 在 AI 领域，我想我们得先加个限定条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are some Legos that shouldn't be given away.
zh: 有些乐高是不应该送出去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just some work that shouldn't be outsourced.
zh: 就是有些工作不应该外包出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a radical departure from your advice over the many years.
zh: 这跟你多年来给的建议是一个彻底的背离。

speaker: Unknown
en: You individually are phenomenal at a set of things, don't outsource it to these weird robots that are effectively summer interns.
zh: 你个人在一组事情上非常出色，不要把它外包给这些实际上相当于暑期实习生的奇怪机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is taking a lot of our Legos, whether we like it or not, and we're being encouraged to give away our Legos to AI.
zh: 不管我们愿不愿意，AI 正在拿走我们很多乐高，而且我们正被鼓励把我们的乐高送给 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had someone on who talked about the job used to be rowing and now it's steering, and I was like, I feel like there's a lot of people out in the world right now that are like, I don't want to steer.
zh: 你邀请过一位嘉宾，他说以前的工作是划桨，现在是掌舵，我当时就想，我觉得现在世界上有很多人是这么想的：我不想掌舵。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard from a lot of engineers just like, I really miss what it used to be.
zh: 我听到很多工程师说，我真的很怀念以前的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Change sucks.
zh: 改变很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also can be awesome, but we don't have to be fluffy bunnies about this, we can also just say this is hard.
zh: 改变也可以很棒，但我们不必在这个问题上装傻卖萌，我们也可以直说这很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is almost a discussion around what should AI do?
zh: 这几乎是一场关于 AI 应该做什么的讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you want AI to be involved and where do you not want it involved?
zh: 你希望 AI 参与到哪里，又不希望它参与到哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you do if you believed your job was always going to exist, it was just going to look completely different every six years?
zh: 如果你相信你的工作会永远存在，只是每六年就会完全变一个样子，你会怎么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Today my guest is Molly Graham.
zh: 今天我的嘉宾是 Molly Graham。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Molly's second visit to the podcast, and man, this is a powerful conversation.
zh: 这是 Molly 第二次来到本播客，天哪，这是一场非常有力量的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: The frame for this conversation is her classic, "Give away your legos" career advice.
zh: 这场对话的框架是她经典的「送出你的乐高」职业建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in an AI world, Molly's advice for the last 13 years has been that your career will be better off if you give away your projects and your teams and your responsibilities to other people as your company grows, versus trying to hold onto it, which is what we naturally want to do.
zh: 但在一个 AI 的世界里，Molly 过去 13 年来的建议一直是：随着你公司的成长，如果你把你的项目、你的团队和你的职责送给其他人，你的职业发展会更好，而不是试图抓住不放——而抓住不放正是我们本能上想做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially to give away your Legos.
zh: 本质上就是送出你的乐高。

speaker: Unknown
en: After 13 years of giving this advice and it unlocking so much win for so many people over the past decade, Molly's realized that it is no longer true when you are giving away your Legos to AI.
zh: 在给出这个建议 13 年、并在过去十年里为这么多人解锁了如此多成功之后，Molly 意识到，当你是把乐高送给 AI 时，这条建议不再成立了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a lot more nuanced and complicated now.
zh: 现在的情况要细致和复杂得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, in this conversation, we try to get to the bottom of this question, what Legos should you still be giving away and what Legos should you keep?
zh: 所以在这场对话中，我们试图弄清这个问题的底细：哪些乐高你仍然应该送出去，哪些乐高你应该留住？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're not familiar with Molly, she has spent 20 plus years helping organizations and the humans inside them navigate growth and change.
zh: 如果你不熟悉 Molly，她花了 20 多年时间帮助各种组织以及组织内的人们应对成长与变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's held leadership roles at Google, and Facebook, and Quip, and the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.
zh: 她在 Google、Facebook、Quip 以及 Chan Zuckerberg Initiative 担任过领导职务。

speaker: Unknown
en: These days, she hosts Ted's Work Life podcast, which she took over from Adam Grant.
zh: 如今，她主持 Ted 的 Work Life 播客，这个节目是她从 Adam Grant 手里接手的。

speaker: Unknown
en: She also runs an incredibly important leadership community called Glue Club, and writes a newsletter called Lessons.
zh: 她还运营着一个极其重要的领导力社区，叫 Glue Club，并撰写一份叫 Lessons 的通讯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, before we get into it, I noticed a lot of people don't finish our full episodes and miss some of the best stuff.
zh: 现在，在我们开始之前，我注意到很多人没有听完我们的完整单集，错过了最好的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, to help you, we've just created a new Lenny's Most Replayed Moments YouTube channel that has exactly this, the most re-watched and shared segments from our long form episodes.
zh: 所以，为了帮到你，我们刚刚创建了一个新的 Lenny's Most Replayed Moments YouTube 频道，里面正是这些内容——我们长篇单集中被重看和分享最多的片段。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can now check it out and subscribe to the channel at lennyspodcast.com/mostreplayedmoments.
zh: 你现在可以去 lennyspodcast.com/mostreplayedmoments 看看并订阅这个频道。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also a link in the description.
zh: 说明区里也有链接。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finally, don't forget to check out lennysproductpass.com for a free year of the hottest and most beautifully crafted AI and non-AI products in the world.
zh: 最后，别忘了去 lennysproductpass.com 看看，可以获得一年免费的世界最热门、打磨最精美的 AI 和非 AI 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's lennysproductpass.com.
zh: 网址是 lennysproductpass.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that, I bring you Molly Graham.
zh: 那么，有请 Molly Graham。

speaker: Unknown
en: Molly, thank you so much for being here and welcome back to the podcast.
zh: Molly，非常感谢你来到这里，欢迎回到本播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me, Lenny.
zh: 谢谢你邀请我，Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm excited to be back.
zh: 我很兴奋能回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm even more excited to have you back.
zh: 我更兴奋能请你回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me add a little context to this slightly unusual conversation we're going to have.
zh: 让我为这场稍微不太寻常的对话补充一点背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, we've been chatting over the past couple months about your famous, infamous give away your Legos career advice, and this question came up, and I know you're hearing this a lot from other people, this idea of how this advice applies in today's very strange AI world, where AI is taking a lot of our Legos, whether we like it or not.
zh: 过去几个月我们一直在聊你那个著名又「声名狼藉」的「送出你的乐高」职业建议，然后这个问题冒出来了——我知道你也经常从别人那里听到这个问题——就是这个建议如何应用在当今这个非常奇怪的 AI 世界里，在这个世界里，不管我们愿不愿意，AI 正在拿走我们很多乐高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're being encouraged to give our Legos to AI, people are afraid about AI taking their Legos.
zh: 而且我们正被鼓励把我们的乐高送给 AI，人们害怕 AI 拿走他们的乐高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, the question is just how this advice now applies in a world of AI.
zh: 所以问题就是：这个建议如今在 AI 的世界里该如何应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know this is kind of an ongoing thought process for you, but you actually have a lot of really interesting insights and takes on how to think about this advice now in today's very strange world.
zh: 我知道这对你来说是一个还在进行中的思考过程，但关于如何在当今这个非常奇怪的世界里看待这条建议，你其实有很多非常有趣的洞见和观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, we're going to have a conversation about it, see where it goes.
zh: 所以我们就来聊一聊，看看会聊到哪里。

en: Literally every startup that I'm an investor in that starts to expand upmarket ends up working with WorkOS, and that's because they are the best.
zh: 说真的，我投资的每一家开始向上市场扩张的初创公司，最终都用上了 WorkOS，那是因为他们是最棒的。

en: Whether you are a seed stage startup trying to land your first enterprise customer or a unicorn expanding globally, WorkOS is the fastest path to becoming enterprise ready and unblocking growth.

en: It's essentially Stripe for enterprise features.

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit workos.com to get started or just hit up their Slack where they have actual engineers waiting to answer your questions.
zh: 访问 workos.com 开始使用，或者直接去他们的 Slack，那里有真正的工程师等着回答你的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: WorkOS allows you to build faster with delightful APIs, comprehensive docs, and a smooth developer experience.
zh: WorkOS 让你用令人愉悦的 API、全面的文档和流畅的开发者体验更快地构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to workos.com to make your app enterprise ready today.
zh: 前往 workos.com，让你的应用今天就达到企业级就绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd say as a first step, let's remind people what this advice is.
zh: 我想，作为第一步，先提醒大家这条建议是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine most people have heard it, a lot of people are probably like, "Oh yeah, I kind of get the idea."
zh: 我想象大多数人已经听说过，很多人可能会说：“哦对，我大概明白这个意思。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So, explain the original idea of giving away your Legos.
zh: 那么，请解释一下“送走你的乐高”这个原始想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually started when I was at Google and Facebook, and it started as a little talk that I would give people that worked for me.
zh: 它实际上始于我在 Google 和 Facebook 的时候，最初只是我给为我工作的人做的一个小分享。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for context, Google was pretty big when I joined, it was like 10,000 employees in 2007, but my department grew from 25 people to 125 people in nine months.
zh: 给点背景，我加入时 Google 已经相当大了，2007 年大约有 10000 名员工，但我的部门在九个月内从 25 人增长到 125 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, that was my first experience with really rapid scale.
zh: 所以那是我第一次经历真正快速的规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I went to Facebook, and Facebook was relatively small when I joined, it was 500 employees, and 80 million users...
zh: 然后我去了 Facebook，我加入时 Facebook 相对较小，只有 500 名员工，8000 万用户……

speaker: Unknown
en: Smaller than MySpace, which is always good context to remember.
zh: 比 MySpace 还小，这个背景值得一直记着。

speaker: Unknown
en: And while I was there, obviously a huge growth curve.
zh: 而我在那里期间，显然是巨大的增长曲线。

speaker: Unknown
en: I left five years later, it was 5,500 employees and over a billion users.
zh: 五年后我离开时，已有 5500 名员工和超过十亿用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, that experience was nuts from a scaling perspective, and what I witnessed at Google and then really witnessed at Facebook was how hard and scary that experience was for people.
zh: 所以从规模化的角度来看，那段经历太疯狂了，我在 Google 见证到、然后真正在 Facebook 见证到的是，那段经历对人们来说有多艰难、多可怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: I watched a lot of folks go from you build a thing... You show up and you become the person that owns the blog, or owns this part of the stack, or built that product, and you sort of build an identity around it.
zh: 我看着很多人从“你做了一个东西”……你来上班，然后成为拥有博客的那个人，或者拥有技术栈的某一部分，或者做了那个产品，然后你围绕它建立了一种身份认同。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're the this person, whatever that is.
zh: 你是那个什么什么的人，不管那是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the nature of scale is that everything around you changes.
zh: 而规模化的本质就是你周围的一切都在变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so somebody shows up and your manager shows up and says, "Hey, you need to hand that thing that you built your whole identity around to someone else and go on to doing something else."
zh: 于是有人出现了，你的经理出现并说：“嘿，你需要把那个你围绕着它建立了整个身份认同的东西交给别人，然后去做别的事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And your first instinct is like, what?
zh: 你的第一反应是：什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I don't want to give it away.
zh: 不，我不想把它送出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm good at this, I know how to do this.
zh: 我擅长这个，我知道怎么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think it's fun, and what if it's the only fun thing to do?
zh: 而且我觉得这很有趣，万一这是唯一有趣的事呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you kind of witness people would have this tendency to hold on.
zh: 所以，你会看到人们有一种想抓住不放的倾向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, what I started to do with people on my team was say, "Hey, this change is happening and here's how you might feel."
zh: 于是，我开始对团队里的人说：“嘿，这种变化正在发生，以下是你可能的感受。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That you might feel like all these feelings, territorial and wanting to hold on, and actually the most important thing to do is to give things away.
zh: 你可能会有这一堆感受，地盘意识、想抓住不放，而实际上最重要的事情是把东西送出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: To evolve as the company is evolving.
zh: 随着公司的演变而演变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my brain is a really weird place.
zh: 而且我的大脑是个很奇怪的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I grew up on The Muppets, so I just spits out...
zh: 我是看《芝麻街》（The Muppets）长大的，所以我会随口蹦出……

speaker: Unknown
en: I always think there's just a lot of tiny monsters dancing around singing songs in my head, but that is why metaphors come out for me.
zh: 我总觉得脑子里有很多小怪物在跳舞唱歌，这就是为什么我总会冒出隐喻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I always use this metaphor of just a bunch of kindergartners and somebody dumps a pile of Legos in front of you, and at first it's fun, a little overwhelming, then you start building.
zh: 所以我总是用这个隐喻：一群幼儿园小朋友，有人在你面前倒下一堆乐高，起初很好玩，有点让人不知所措，然后你开始搭建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the give away your Legos part is that feeling when somebody else shows up, and they try to take the tower out of your hands.
zh: 而“送走你的乐高”指的就是那种感觉：当别人出现，想从你手里把塔拿走。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the kindergartner response is like, "Get out of here."
zh: 而幼儿园小朋友的反应是：“走开。”

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what I mean?
zh: 你懂我的意思吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, shoving someone away, when actually you get multiple people, it means, oh, you can go build something new and fun.
zh: 就是把人推开，但实际上有更多人来，意味着：哦，你可以去做新的、好玩的东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can start from scratch and you can learn something.
zh: 你可以从零开始，你可以学到新东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the natural human instinct in the face of change is to hold onto things and to resist the change, to be territorial and all of those things.
zh: 但面对变化，人的本能就是抓住东西不放、抗拒变化、有地盘意识，等等这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, anyway, I started giving this talk to folks on my team to help them understand that change and what was coming, and then eventually I sent it out to my friends at First Round, who were building the First Round Review at the time... And just to be clear, this is now 13 years ago.
zh: 所以，后来我开始给我的团队成员做这个分享，帮助他们理解这种变化以及即将到来的事情，最终我把它发给了我在 First Round 的朋友们，他们当时正在创办 First Round Review……要说明一下，那已经是 13 年前了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The talk when I was at Facebook, it was over 20 years ago.
zh: 我在 Facebook 做那个分享时，是 20 多年前了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I sent it to First Round, and we published it.
zh: 我把它发给了 First Round，然后我们发表了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would've said I was speaking to folks going through a Facebook-like experience, I would've said, hey, this is an article that is for the Stripes or the Slacks or whoever was blowing up in 2013, to normalize, hey, this is what it feels like and this is what you have to do to grow as fast as your company is growing.
zh: 如果说我是讲给正在经历 Facebook 式体验的人听的，我会说，嘿，这是一篇写给 Stripe、Slack 或者 2013 年那些正在爆发的公司的文章，为了让这件事正常化：嘿，这就是那种感受，这就是你要做的事，才能跟得上公司增长的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what happened when it was published is that I got emails from all over the world.
zh: 但文章发表后发生的事情是，我收到了来自世界各地的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got emails from people at companies like Safeway, and this woman, I still remember this email, wrote me and was like, "This was so helpful to me.
zh: 我收到来自 Safeway 这类公司的人的邮件，有一位女士，我至今还记得那封邮件，她写道：“这对我来说太有帮助了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This perfectly describes what I've been going through on my team."
zh: 这完美描述了我团队里正在经历的事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I got an email, again, I remember it very vividly from a founder in Nigeria, who was like, "My team went from two people to four people this year, and give away your Legos is so valuable to me.
zh: 我还收到一封邮件，我同样记得非常清楚，来自尼日利亚的一位创始人，他说：“我的团队今年从两个人变成了四个人，‘送走你的乐高’对我来说太宝贵了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is exactly what I've been feeling."
zh: “这正是我一直以来的感受。"

speaker: Unknown
en: And my first reaction was like, "I didn't write this for you, this was not meant for you."
zh: 我的第一反应是：“我又不是写给你的，这本来不是给你看的。"

speaker: Unknown
en: But my second one was, "Whoa, this is about something much bigger than just what it feels like to be inside of rapid scale."
zh: 但我的第二个反应是：“哇，这讲的是比身处快速扩张之中的感受要大得多的东西。"

speaker: Unknown
en: And fundamentally, I think the Legos message is about change, and it's about the fact that when you go through change, a lot of happens to you.
zh: 从根本上说，我认为 Legos 这篇文章讲的是变化，讲的是当你经历变化时，你身上会发生很多事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what I mean?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It just is a very specific experience, and I think that's why it ended up being so universal.
zh: 它就是一种非常具体的体验，我想这就是为什么它最终变得如此具有普适性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is crazy, I still get emails about it, multiple emails a month about it to this day.
zh: 而且很疯狂的是，我至今仍然会收到关于它的邮件，每个月都有好几封。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it's lasted in a way that, again, I just thought I was sending out a note to the folks that are going through crazy rapid change.
zh: 所以，它以一种方式延续了下来——再次强调，我当时只是以为自己是在给那些正经历疯狂快速变化的人发一封短信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was at a first round event, I don't know, a year ago or something, and they were talking about all the different posts people have written, and I think it's one of the, maybe the first or second most popular post on the First Round Review
zh: 我大概一年前参加了一个 First Round 的活动，他们在谈大家写过的各种文章，我想它是最受欢迎的、也许排第一或第二的文章之一，在 First Round Review 上

speaker: Unknown
en: It's up there and it's traveled in ways that I don't think any of us imagined it would.
zh: 它就在那里，而且它的传播之广，超出了我们任何人的想象。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let's talk about what still holds true in this advice in this today's very strange AI world.
zh: 那么，我们来谈谈在如今这个非常奇怪的 AI 世界里，这些建议中哪些仍然成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: What still holds true?
zh: 哪些仍然成立？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's still correct about this advice based on what you're seeing?
zh: 根据你观察到的情况，这些建议中哪些仍然是对的？

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that's crazy about this article is I still get so many emails about it today.
zh: 关于这篇文章有一件很疯狂的事，就是我到今天仍然收到那么多关于它的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I still get asked to give speeches at every fast-growing company.
zh: 我仍然被每一家快速增长的公司邀请去做演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think for anybody that's going through rapid scale, Legos is still really relevant.
zh: 所以我认为，对于任何正在经历快速扩张的人来说，Legos 仍然非常相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the interesting thing is what started to happen probably two years ago is I got more inbound from managers, and more inbound from leaders about Legos, just more people grappling with change inside their companies.
zh: 但有意思的是，大概两年前开始发生的事情是，我收到越来越多来自管理者、越来越多来自领导者的关于 Legos 的主动联络，只是有更多人在他们公司内部与变化苦苦抗争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is the thing that really holds true today and actually has just become more universal.
zh: 我认为这是今天真正站得住脚的东西，而且实际上已经变得更加普适了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to really check before I went and did a speech at some company, how fast the company was growing, I would ask about revenue growth and about headcount growth... Because that just helps me contextualize how I should speak to employees.
zh: 我以前去某家公司做演讲之前，真的会先核实一下，了解这家公司增长有多快，我会问营收增长和人数增长的情况……因为这能帮助我确定该用怎样的方式对员工讲话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I still do that, but it's also become really clear that every single company in the world is going through enormous change of varying shapes and kinds right now.
zh: 我现在仍然这么做，但同样变得非常清楚的一点是，如今世界上每一家公司都在经历不同形态、不同种类的巨大变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is the fundamental underlying message of Legos, is how do you deal with change and how do you be your best self in the face of change?
zh: 而这正是 Legos 最根本的底层信息：你如何应对变化，你如何在变化面前做最好的自己？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I feel like the number one thing that is true today, as true as it was 10 or 15 years ago, is the change is really scary and hard.
zh: 所以，我觉得今天成立的第一件事，和 10 年或 15 年前一样成立，就是变化真的很可怕、很艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I always say, somebody once asked me to summarize the Legos article in one sentence, they're like, "Molly, this is too long, give me the cliff notes," and I said two things.
zh: 我总是说，有一次有人让我用一句话总结 Legos 这篇文章，他们说：“Molly，这也太长了，给我精华版吧。"我说了两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unfortunately, they didn't get one sentence, they got two.
zh: 可惜，他们没得到一句话，得到了两句。

speaker: Unknown
en: The two sentences were, number one, your main job in the face of rapid growth and change is to make yourself irrelevant because it is the only way that you can be prepared for whatever is coming next.
zh: 这两句是：第一，面对快速增长和变化时，你的主要工作是让自己变得不再被需要，因为这是你为接下来到来的任何事情做好准备的唯一方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second piece of advice, or sort of second summary of it was, don't worry, it's all going to be okay.
zh: 第二条建议，或者说对它的第二种总结是：别担心，一切都会好起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always feel like the Legos article and the speeches I give are like a form of group therapy.
zh: 我一直觉得 Legos 这篇文章和我做的演讲就像一种团体治疗。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like just a giant hug.
zh: 它们就像一个大大的拥抱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, it feels chaotic and overwhelming and stressful, but there's all this opportunity on the other side.
zh: 是的，感觉混乱、不堪重负、压力巨大，但另一边有这一切的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the don't worry, it's all going to be okay is really something everybody needs to hear, that change is scary and hard, but it doesn't necessarily mean the world is ending.
zh: 我认为“别担心，一切都会好起来的”真的是每个人都需要听到的话——变化很可怕、很艰难，但这并不一定意味着世界末日。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the second piece of that is that change comes with this incredible set of emotions, like this wild roller coaster that we don't talk about enough.
zh: 我认为第二点在于，变化伴随着这一整套难以置信的情绪，就像一趟狂野的过山车，而我们对它谈论得不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that was a lot of why I first started talking about Legos at Facebook and on my teams was I just wanted to normalize for people what it felt like.
zh: 我想，这也是我当初开始在 Facebook 以及在我的团队里谈论 Legos 的一大原因，我就是想让人们把这感受正常化。

speaker: Unknown
en: That you might feel all these feelings and that that was what everyone around you was feeling, that it didn't make you crazy and it didn't make you broken or something like that.
zh: 你可能会有这所有这些感受，而这正是你周围每个人都在感受的，这不会让你疯狂，也不会让你破碎或类似的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also didn't mean anything was wrong, it actually meant that all the right things were happening.
zh: 它也不意味着有什么地方出了问题，实际上它意味着所有对的事情正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is very real today.
zh: 而我认为这在今天依然非常真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I travel around and I'm talking to leaders, and I know you and I are going to talk about this, but a lot of what I'm hearing is grief and all these different emotions.
zh: 当我四处奔走、与领导者们交谈时——我知道你和我接下来会谈到这个——我听到的大部分是悲伤和各种不同的情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's obviously excitement and joy in this moment of chaos and change with AI, but there is a lot of sadness.
zh: 在 AI 带来的这个混乱与变化时刻，显然有兴奋和喜悦，但也有大量的悲伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of overwhelm that all manifests, some of it manifests in burnout.
zh: 有大量的不堪重负，它们以各种方式显现，其中一些表现为职业倦怠。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's like there is just a lot going on for people right now, and you really can't lead right now without talking about that and without normalizing that.
zh: 但现在人们身上就是有太多事情在发生，而你现在如果不谈论这些、不把这些正常化，就真的无法领导。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's such a big part of the give away your Legos today is just helping people understand that these emotions are just part of your body and your identity reacting to change.
zh: 我认为这正是今天“交出你的 Legos”很重要的一大组成部分，就是帮助人们理解，这些情绪只是你的身体和你的身份认同对变化作出的反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other two things I would say that really do still feel true to me, that I both talk about in the article and have talked about a lot since is one of the things I say to people that are inside of a really rapidly growing company is the future will be defined by the people that learn, not the people that know.
zh: 另外两件我觉得至今仍然非常真实的事，我在文章里都谈过，之后也谈过很多，其中之一是，我对那些身处一家真正快速增长公司里的人说的话是：未来将由学习的人定义，而不是由知道的人定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always say, what you can learn by tomorrow matters way more than what you know today.
zh: 我总是说，你到明天为止能学到的东西，远比你今天已经知道的东西重要得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And never has a truer sentence been said than about the age of AI.
zh: 而关于 AI 时代，再没有比这更真实的一句话了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what I mean?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever we though we knew six months ago, toss it out the window, something new is true today.
zh: 我们六个月前以为自己知道的任何东西，都扔出窗外吧，今天有新的东西是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I used to say to people, and I still say, I guess when I do these speeches is you go look at that graph of how fast your company is growing.
zh: 但我过去常对人们说、现在做这些演讲时我猜也还在说的是：你去看看那张你们公司增长速度有多快的图。

speaker: Unknown
en: You go look at that curve... And at Facebook it felt like we were falling off of it.
zh: 你去看看那条曲线……在 Facebook，我们感觉自己正在从那条曲线上掉下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the graph of how fast your company is growing, yes, but it is also the graph of how fast your job is growing, how fast every single thing around you is growing and changing, which means it's also the graph of how fast you need to grow.
zh: 那是你公司增长速度的图，没错，但它也是你的工作增长速度的图，是你身边每一件事物增长和变化速度的图，这意味着它也是你需要以多快的速度成长的图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is such an important thing to understand inside of a world of change, which is that standing still, it feels safe, it feels like to hold onto what you know, because at least it's not scary and unknown.
zh: 我认为在一个变化的世界里，理解这一点非常重要，那就是原地不动，感觉上是安全的，感觉像是抓住你已经知道的东西不放，因为至少它不吓人、不是未知的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But actually standing still is the least safe thing you can do.
zh: 但实际上原地踏步才是你能做的最不安全的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's basically you're guaranteed to fall behind.
zh: 这基本上意味着你注定会落后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I saw this viscerally at Facebook because the first two years I was in HR, and you could literally see the highest performer one year, if they didn't grow and change and if they didn't involve their team fast enough, they were underwater less than a year later because it was a different company.
zh: 我在 Facebook 曾切身感受到这一点，因为我头两年在 HR 部门，你能真真切切地看到，某一年的最高绩效者，如果他们没有成长和改变，如果他们没有足够快地推动他们的团队进化，不到一年之后他们就落水了，因为那已经是一家不同的公司了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this is happening with AI as well, which is that we do have these instincts to hold on to what we know, and to defend what we know, and to fight for what we know for a bunch of different reasons, many of them good, but the future is going to be defined by the people that are willing to just take the stance of learning and to throw themselves into this change, scary and unknown as it is.
zh: 我认为 AI 领域也在发生同样的事情，出于各种不同的原因，我们确实有这种本能去抓住我们所知道的、捍卫我们所知道的、为我们所知道的而奋斗，其中很多理由是好的，但未来将由那些愿意采取学习姿态、愿意把自己投入到这场变革中的人来定义，无论它多么可怕和未知。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that message again remains true in this wild, wild world.
zh: 而且这个道理在这个狂野、狂野的世界里依然成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get into just how the advice is different, which when you go back to your summary of the two kind of items that summarize the idea, one is become redundant and then two, what was the second sentence?
zh: 在我们深入探讨这个建议具体有何不同之前——当你回到你对那两条总结要点的概括时，一条是变得冗余，然后第二条是什么来着？

speaker: Molly Graham
en: The second one is basically don't worry, it's all going to be okay.
zh: 第二条基本上是：别担心，一切都会好起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't worry.
zh: 别担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, those don't feel necessarily correct anymore.
zh: 所以，这些感觉已经不一定正确了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, we're going to get into that because I think that's, as you said, the core of people's concern.
zh: 所以我们要深入探讨这个，因为我觉得，正如你所说，这正是人们担忧的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was comforting, and now it's like, well, are you sure?
zh: 这原本是种安慰，现在却变成了，嗯，你确定吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This grief piece, just to spend a little more time here, I've been seeing this a lot in a lot of different professions, I've done these surveys that we might get into a little bit, but just engineering as a role has completely transformed in two years.
zh: 关于悲伤这部分，再多花一点时间说，我在很多不同的职业中都看到了这一点，我做过一些我们稍后可能会谈到的调查，但光是工程师这个角色在两年内已经彻底转变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been like the same job forever, writing code, sitting there writing code in various forms of IDEs, no longer part of the job.
zh: 一直以来都是同样的工作，写代码，坐在那里以各种形式的 IDE 写代码，这已经不再是这份工作的一部分了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now it's talking to your AI to write the code.
zh: 现在是跟你的 AI 对话来写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether you're there or not, that's where it's all going.
zh: 无论你是否在场，这就是一切的发展方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be 100% write this thing, build this thing.
zh: 未来将是 100% 的：写下这个东西，构建这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I used to be an engineer, and I moved into product, and I was so missing that flow state of being an engineer, just sitting there coding, building, and now that's gone.
zh: 我以前是工程师，后来转向了产品，我曾非常怀念工程师的那种心流状态，就是坐在那里写代码、构建东西，而现在那种状态已经没有了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You no longer sit there and just build a thing, you're just waiting for agents to run and then checking, you probably have 100 different agents, it's just a very strange new job.
zh: 你不再坐在那里只是构建一个东西，你只是在等智能体运行然后检查，你可能有 100 个不同的智能体，这是一个非常奇怪的新工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've heard from a lot of engineers just like, "I really miss what it used to be."
zh: 我听到很多工程师说：“我真的怀念过去的样子。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything more there about just, I don't know, what you're hearing from folks about just like, man, this sucks?
zh: 关于这个还有更多想说的吗，就是，我不知道，你从大家那里听到的关于，天哪，这太糟了之类的感受？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's exactly...
zh: 是的，这正是……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's such a perfect example of the grief.
zh: 这是悲伤的一个完美例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was giving a speech two weeks ago at a pretty fast-growing tech company, and this guy came up to me after and he'd been at the company for a couple of years, so it's gone through a huge amount of change.
zh: 两周前我在一家增长相当快的科技公司做演讲，演讲后有个小伙子找到我，他在那家公司待了几年了，所以经历了巨大的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he was talking to me about the fact that he just wasn't enjoying his role as much anymore.
zh: 他跟我说的是，他不再那么享受他的角色了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my brain immediately went to, oh right, you enjoyed it when it was smaller, and there was more creativity, and now there's more structure.
zh: 我脑子里立刻想到，哦对了，公司更小的时候你享受那份工作，那时有更多创造力，现在有更多架构了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I was talking to him about that.
zh: 所以，我跟他聊的是这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it took a while, and to some extent, I want to go talk to him again because I feel like I missed it in the first conversation.
zh: 这花了一段时间，在某种程度上，我想再去跟他谈谈，因为我觉得我在第一次对话中漏掉了重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where actually, I think what he was talking about was the grief that is very present for him now in the fact that he's not sure what is his current job, what is this...
zh: 实际上，我认为他所说的是他现在非常强烈感受到的悲伤，他不确定自己现在的工作是什么，这是什么……

speaker: Unknown
en: The company has grown and so he's in a more structured environment and what is just the simple fact that engineering has totally changed?
zh: 公司成长了，所以他处于一个更有架构的环境里，再加上工程本身已经彻底改变这个简单事实，这些到底是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of what he was talking about was how much he missed being more hands-on, which is one way of saying it.
zh: 他说了很多关于他多么怀念更亲自动手的日子，这是一种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that that grief is happening for a lot of people, I think engineering is probably one of the most visceral areas where people's jobs have genuinely transformed.
zh: 但我认为这种悲伤正发生在很多人身上，我认为工程领域可能是人们的岗位真正发生转变的最切身可感的领域之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had someone on last week who talked about the job used to be rowing and now it's-
zh: 你上周请过一位嘉宾，她说这份工作过去是划船，现在是——

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, Tara, yeah, from OpenAI.
zh: 哦，Tara，对，来自 OpenAI 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: She said the job used to be rowing and now it's like-
zh: 她说这份工作过去是划船，现在更像是——

speaker: Lenny
en: Steering.
zh: 掌舵。

speaker: Unknown
en: Steering.
zh: 掌舵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, I feel like there's a lot of people out in the world right now that are like, I don't want to fucking steer.
zh: 然后我当时就想，我觉得现在世界上有很多人心里在想，我他妈的不想掌舵。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what I mean?
zh: 你懂我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to row.
zh: 我想划船。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like rowing.
zh: 我喜欢划船。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it can be hard to separate, I like rowing or I'm scared that rowing is the only thing I'm ever going to be good at, or it's what I know, and I don't know if I can be good at steering.
zh: 而且我觉得很难分清，是我喜欢划船，还是我害怕划船是我唯一擅长的事情，或者那是我所熟悉的，而我不知道自己能否擅长掌舵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's happening in a lot of disciplines.
zh: 我认为这在很多领域都在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, that grief, first and foremost, that grief is really real.
zh: 所以，那种悲伤，首先要说的就是，那种悲伤是真实存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was talking to a product leader just the other day who was like, "I don't know, man, we're all supposed to be these universal builders now," and she was like, "It's kind of lonely."
zh: 前几天我刚跟一位产品负责人聊过，她说：“我不知道啊，老兄，我们现在都应该成为这种全能构建者，”然后她说：“这有点孤独。”

speaker: Unknown
en: She's like, "I miss these parts of the collaboration that have been a little bit stripped away because now I'm working with robots all the time."
zh: 她说：“我怀念那些被一定程度剥夺了的协作部分，因为现在我一直在和机器人一起工作。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just said to her, "Yeah man, that sucks.
zh: 而我只是对她说：“是啊老兄，这确实很糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's sit with it for a second.
zh: 我们先在这里待一会儿，好好感受它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Change sucks."
zh: 改变很糟糕。"

speaker: Unknown
en: It also can be awesome, but we don't have to be fluffy bunnies about this, we can also just say this is hard.
zh: 它也可以很棒,但我们不必装作可爱的小兔子,我们也可以直说:这很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much power in just saying the thing that you're feeling.
zh: 把你的感受直说出来,这里面有巨大的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I swear to God that that is a big chunk of what the Legos article did, was just like, this is hard and scary and it's going to be okay.
zh: 我向上帝发誓,那篇 Legos 文章很大程度上做的就是这件事,就是在说:这很难、很可怕,但一切都会好起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This loneliness piece is such an important part to touch on.

zh: 我觉得现在最需要培养的最大技能是，当你正要做某件事时，问自己：“AI 能帮我做这件事吗？”

zh: 因为一旦你在这方面变强了，而且我一直在变得……

speaker: Unknown
en: They're walls, they're old.
zh: 它们是墙，它们很旧了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of what we need to do, and I think part of what you're saying is you're actually little bit at an advantage if you don't know those walls exist.
zh: 我们需要做的一部分事情，我想也是你所说的一部分，是如果你不知道那些墙的存在，你其实反而有一点优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you approach the world as if engineers didn't have a different role from X or Y or Z, or this is the way things are done, there is an advantage to being able to say, "What if?
zh: 如果你以工程师和 X 或 Y 或 Z 没有不同角色、或者事情就该这样做的方式来看待世界，那么能够说出“如果呢？”是一种优势。

en: What if I just did it?"
zh: “如果我就直接做了呢？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And to just try.
zh: 然后就去尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to your point to always think, "Hey, what's the best use of my time?
zh: 而且按你的观点，要始终思考：“嘿，怎么才是我时间最好的利用方式？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what could an agent or a robot do for me?"
zh: 然后一个智能体或机器人能为我做什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's partially the point about the learners.
zh: 我认为这在一定程度上就是关于学习者的关键所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're able to shed the sort of things you think you know and lean into the possibility and the first principles thinking, which I know you have a great article about too, that I think is going to define the future.
zh: 如果你能够放下那些你自以为已经知道的东西，并拥抱可能性与第一性原理思考——我知道你也写过一篇关于这个的非常好的文章——我认为这将定义未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are going to be the people that are going to shape what this thing looks like.
zh: 那些人将是塑造这个东西未来面貌的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们需要的是……

zh: 因为这些工具现在能做太多了，它们只是在等着你告诉我一些比这更有雄心的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's all you got for me?
zh: 你就只有这些给我了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And human nature doesn't... We're not used to end product teams and business just thinking about the most ambitious version of a thing.
zh: 而人性并不……我们还不习惯让产品团队和企业直接去思考一个东西最有雄心的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're thinking about the MVP and what's the quickest way to get this out, and now it feels like the push is how do we think big?
zh: 我们想的是 MVP，想的是最快把这个东西推出去的路径，而现在感觉推动的方向是：我们该如何往大处想？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the hardest thing we can ask this AI to do because it may actually just achieve it out of one ask.
zh: 我们能问这个 AI 去做的最难的事情是什么，因为它可能真的会一次性就把这事做成。

zh: 而且我还想在“你只需把东西打字打出来”这个想法上再推一把：你还需要问自己的另一个问题是，它好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what I mean?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the slop and the accountability thing, which is like... And if ambition is wrapped up in how do I build something phenomenal that's going to endure, that I'm interested in.
zh: 这就是关于垃圾内容和责任的问题，就像是……如果雄心被包裹在“我如何构建一个非凡的、能够长存的东西、一个我感兴趣的东西”里。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's just like, how do I make more shit and put it out in the world?
zh: 如果它只是“我怎么制造更多垃圾然后把它们扔到世界上”？

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my questions, this is really frontier, Lenny, is what is the AI slop version of startups?
zh: 我的问题之一——Lenny，这真的很前沿——什么是创业公司的 AI 垃圾内容版本？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we about to see a shit-ton of companies just shipping stuff out into the world that's going to last for six or 12 months and then just disappear or get irrelevant?
zh: 我们是不是即将看到一大堆公司不断把东西发布到世界上，这些东西只会存活六到十二个月，然后就消失或变得无关紧要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely.
zh: 肯定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So okay, great.
zh: 那好，行吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: That doesn't sound fun.
zh: 这听起来可不怎么有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can you be the pioneer of the enduring thing, the thing that's going to still be around in five years, that's going to matter, that's going to be great, not just exist?
zh: 你要如何成为那个能够长存的东西的先驱——那个五年后仍然存在的东西，那个重要的东西，那个伟大的东西，而不仅仅是存在？

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, it goes to the difference between just productivity, like I built a thing, and what is good?
zh: 再说一次，这就是“仅仅生产力，比如我做出了一个东西”与“什么是好的”之间的区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is actually worth it?
zh: 什么才是真正值得的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's worth other people's time?
zh: 什么值得别人的时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a big differentiating opportunity right now instead of just shipping the thing fast, it's what's a very good version of this thing.
zh: 我认为这是现在一个很大的差异化机会：不是仅仅快速发布这个东西，而是“这个东西的一个非常好的版本是什么”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people see that.
zh: 而且人们会看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, "Oh, wow.
zh: 他们会说：“哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is different."
zh: 这不一样。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this goes to the point of what will matter when it comes to human touch, and I think a lot of that is going to come down to the question of what is good and what is worth it and what endures.
zh: 我认为这触及了人的温度将在哪里起作用这一点，而我认为其中很多将归结为这些问题：什么是好的、什么值得、什么能长存。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything that we haven't touched on that we should before we try to summarize maybe some key lessons from this freewheeling conversation?
zh: 在我们尝试总结这场自由漫谈的一些关键要点之前，还有没有什么我们没有触及但应该谈到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the one thing I just wanted to say is...
zh: 嗯，我只是想说一件事……

speaker: Unknown
en: I was thinking yesterday because of the conversation I was having is like, what do I want every manager or leader out there to know?
zh: 我昨天在想，因为我当时参与的对话，就是：我想让外面每一位管理者或领导者都知道什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think the world of the IC is honestly a little more clear.

speaker: Unknown
en: You are more productive and you have all this power and agency around building, and the world that feels very hard to me right now is the world of the managers and the leaders because so much is changing so fast.

zh: 有点难以知道该告诉人们什么。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means that how you use AI trickles down, but also how you sit in this moment, how you show up.
zh: 这意味着你如何使用 AI 会层层向下渗透，但你如何身处这个时刻、你如何展现自己，也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, what I want a little more space for in the world is to be able to acknowledge what this change feels like.
zh: 而对我而言，我想在这个世界上为“能够承认这场变革给人的感受”争取多一点空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope there's more managers out there because of this conversation talking about grief and talking about the emotions that come with change and talking about how hard this is for people.

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that acknowledging what this rate of change does to people's brains and psychologies, it just...
zh: 我认为，承认这种变化速度对人脑和心理造成了什么，它就是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Honestly, even acknowledging it makes it easier for people.
zh: 说实话，仅仅是承认这一点，就能让人们好受一些。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 就像我说的，我对天发誓，那篇 Legos 文章做的大多数事情就是告诉人们：“嘿，你感受到的那种东西，在你之前其他人也感受过，而且那并不意味着一切都要完蛋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's meant, oh, you're going through a lot of change really, really fast and it's scary and hard."
zh: 它意味着，哦，你正在经历非常、非常快速的变化，这很可怕也很艰难。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So the more that leaders can be talking about that, I think the more sane everyone's going to feel and less alone.
zh: 所以我认为，领导者越多地谈论这一点，每个人就会感觉越理智、越不孤单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Knowing that someone at XYZ company is feeling the same way as you makes a difference.
zh: 知道 XYZ 公司的某个人和你有同样的感受，这很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess the last thing I just say is I think everyone owns this to some extent, but managers and leaders more so, we need to hold on to the definition of accountability and what good means.
zh: 一位出色的管理者所做的就是让人们感到被看见、被支持，并帮助他们理清自己陷入的任何困境。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's part of the role modeling.
zh: 我认为这是榜样示范的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is right to give away to AI and what do we still as humans and people and workers need to own?
zh: 什么是可以交给 AI 的，而我们作为人类、作为人、作为工作者还需要自己承担什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to have to role model that and we're going to have to create standards for that.
zh: 我们将不得不为此做出榜样，我们将不得不为此制定标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that goes to your own behavior, but it also goes to how you lead and how you talk about it.
zh: 所以这关系到你自己的行为，但也关系到你如何领导、如何谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clay put out this beautiful AI writing policy a couple weeks ago, I think it was, and it's so badass because it's literally just talking about being accountable for what you ship out in the world and being accountable for what good is regardless of how you made it.
zh: Clay 几周前发布了一份非常漂亮的 AI 写作政策，我想是的，它非常 badass，因为它字面上就是在谈论为你发布到世界上的东西负责，为“好”的标准负责，无论你是怎么做出它的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for today, to me, that feeling of treating AI as a junior intern and realizing that it's fundamentally just a tool to get work done, but what matters is the work is still done mostly by the humans and the human brains, and we got to take care of the humans and we got to help them figure out how to navigate this wild, wild west that we are in.
zh: 而对今天来说，对我来说，那种把 AI 当作初级实习生对待的感觉，并意识到它从根本上只是一个完成工作的工具，但重要的是工作仍然主要由人类和人类大脑完成，我们必须照顾好人类，我们必须帮助他们弄清楚如何在我们身处的这个狂野西部中航行。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really glad you added that.
zh: 我真的很高兴你补充了那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It connects to another really interesting insight from the survey, which is that the one thing that you can actually change to increase people's happiness right now at work is their manager.

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the strongest lever for happiness at work.
zh: 那是工作幸福感最强的杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can actually do something about it.
zh: 你实际上可以为此做点什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: All this other AI stuff you can't do a ton about, that's one.
zh: 所有其他 AI 相关的东西你做不了太多，但这一件可以。

zh: 而且根据调查，大多数人的管理者并不好。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这些都不令人惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: So taking care of the managers is kind of just a reminder that you have a lot of leverage there as well.
zh: 所以照顾好管理者，有点像是在提醒你，你在那里也有很大的杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, which by the way, there are trends inside of bigger companies to get rid of management, to get rid of whole management layers, and I think it is a huge mistake.
zh: 是的，顺便说一下，大公司里有取消管理、取消整个管理层级的趋势，我认为这是一个巨大的错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it is going to end up biting people in the ass long term because I see no signs right now that management matters less.
zh: 我认为它最终会长期反噬人们，因为我现在看不到任何管理变得不那么重要的迹象。

speaker: Unknown

en: And again, I get the efficiency and the cost savings and all that, but I think at what costs that you can't predict.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: People have had great managers, they're rarely going to be like, "I wish I had no manager."

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the people with bad managers, which a lot of people are like, "I don't need this person, but they're so useless."
zh: 就像那些拥有糟糕管理者的人，很多人会说“我不需要这个人，他们太没用了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, they're in my way.
zh: 是的，他们挡着我的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are a wall.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 不，完全如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I always say you only get a couple good managers in your life and when you find one, hold onto it for dear life because you're only going to get two.
zh: 我是说，我总是说，你一生中只会遇到几个好的管理者，当你找到一个时，要拼了命地抓住它，因为你只会遇到两个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 哦，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scary.
zh: 可怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never heard that advice before.
zh: 我以前从没听过这个建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything else that you wanted to share or touch on?
zh: 还有什么你想分享或谈到的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it'll be fascinating.
zh: 我是说，这将会非常引人入胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll reflect on this in six months and see what-
zh: 我们会在六个月后回顾这一点，看看——

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I was thinking.
zh: 我也是这么想的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in the middle of it right now.
zh: 我们现在正处于其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like Elizabeth Stone had a really good way of framing it.
zh: 就像 Elizabeth Stone 有一个非常好的表述方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in the storming phase and then there's the norming phase.
zh: 我们处于 storming 阶段，然后是 norming 阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have no idea what that actually means, but it sounds right.
zh: 我完全不知道那实际上是什么意思，但听起来是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Storming, norming.
zh: Storming，norming。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, there's storming, norming, and then there's performing.
zh: 嗯，有 storming、norming，然后是 performing。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the other thing that nobody tells you about that framework is that you can go backwards.
zh: 但关于那个框架没人告诉你的是，你可以倒退。

speaker: Unknown
en: You often go through cycles.
zh: 你经常会经历循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a model on team development and you go through storming and then you go through norming and then you go for performing, but you can slip from performing into storming, and I feel like we're going to see a lot of that.
zh: 这是一个关于团队发展的模型，你经历 storming，然后经历 norming，然后进入 performing，但你可以从 performing 滑落回 storming，我感觉我们会看到很多这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, boy.
zh: 哦，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very cool to be living through this history, right?
zh: 能亲身经历这段历史真的很酷，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easy to take for granted just how this is.
zh: 人们很容易把这一切视为理所当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like we're living through history.
zh: 就好像我们正活在历史之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's funny you say that because that's actually something I always talk about when I do these Lego speeches is being inside of a rapidly growing company feels like being inside of a tornado.
zh: 你这么说很有意思，因为这其实是我在做那些乐高演讲时总会谈到的一点：身处一家快速成长的公司里，感觉就像身处一场龙卷风之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what I mean?
zh: 你懂我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like it is so absorbing and I don't know, shit just flying at you at all times and everything's changing all the time.
zh: 就是那种特别让人沉浸的状态，各种破事不断朝你飞来，一切都在不停地变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is so easy in that state to lose the forest for the trees.
zh: 在这种状态下，人很容易只见树木不见森林。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can get really bogged down or stuck in obsessing about this person or this thing or feeling undervalued.
zh: 你可能会陷入对这个人、这件事的纠结，或者觉得自己没被重视，无法自拔。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of what I say to folks in those speeches is you got to zoom out.
zh: 我在那些演讲中对大家说的很多话就是：你得把镜头拉远。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got to think about what is the story that I want to tell on the other side of this?
zh: 你得想一想，在这段经历结束后，我想讲一个什么样的故事？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's less about your title or all these things than it is about, I was here and I helped build this.
zh: 这更多地不是关于你的头衔或这些东西，而是关于，我当时在场，我参与了建设这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talk about it as a giant Lego sculpture.
zh: 我把它比作一个巨大的乐高雕塑。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're like, "Let's pretend it's a tiger".
zh: 所以你就说：“我们假装它是一只老虎”。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to leave here with this incredible story.
zh: 你离开这里的时候会带着这个精彩的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You built the feed and then you were part of building the face and then you rebuilt the butt three times and then you realized it wasn't just a tiger, it was a whole zoo.
zh: 你搭了信息流，然后你参与了搭脸，然后你把屁股重搭了三次，然后你意识到这不只是一只老虎，而是一整个动物园。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is what it feels like to be inside of these rapidly changing companies.
zh: 这就是在这些快速变化的公司里的感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wonder... As you were saying that, what I was thinking about is, gosh, imagine the stories we're going to be telling in five or 10 years.
zh: 而我在想……当你说这些的时候，我在想的是，天哪，想象一下我们在五年或十年后要讲的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was there when, here's what I thought that was right.
zh: 我当时在场，这是我当时的正确想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's what I though that was wrong.
zh: 这是我当时的错误想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was the first person to say this.
zh: 我是第一个说出这句话的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 哦，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was so wrong about that.
zh: 我在那件事上错得太离谱了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are living through history that you will be telling stories about to whatever generation of new grads shows up in 10 years.
zh: 你正在亲历的历史，你会在十年后讲给新入职的那一代毕业生听。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you want your part of that story to be?
zh: 你想在这个故事中扮演什么样的角色？

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you going to tell that story?
zh: 你会怎么讲那个故事？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there is something about zooming out and realizing it is hard and there is a lot of change going on, but there is a crazy fun story that we're all going to be telling on the other side of this.
zh: 我觉得，把镜头拉远并意识到这一点很重要：这确实很难，确实有大量的变化在发生，但等这一切过去之后，我们所有人都会讲一个极其精彩的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just don't know what it is yet.
zh: 我们只是还不知道那会是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hopefully not just talking to our AGI, "Tell me more.
zh: 但愿不只是对着我们的 AGI 说话，“多告诉我一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell me more, Molly."
zh: 多告诉我一些，Molly。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全是。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's so fascinating.
zh: 太有意思了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是啊，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: "You're so great.
zh: “你太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're so smart."
zh: 你太聪明了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 哦，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What if we do just some bullet points, like takeaways for folks, just like here's a few key things to keep in mind coming from this giving away your Legos framework, see where your mind goes and then maybe I'll add a few for my notes.
zh: 要不然我们就列一些要点吧，就是给大家的收获，就比如从“送出你的乐高”这个框架出发，有哪几件关键的事需要记住，看看你的思路会到哪里，然后也许我会给我的笔记再补充几条。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, most important is change is scary and hard, but that doesn't mean it's bad.
zh: 对我来说，最重要的是：变化是可怕且艰难的，但这并不意味着它是坏的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means you have to embrace the emotions that come with it, but you also have to lean into it and you should let go.
zh: 这意味着你必须拥抱随之而来的情绪，但你也必须迎难而上，而且你应该放手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, it's scary and yes, it feels like there may not be anything waiting on the other side, but what's the alternative, to hold on to this thing that might be slowly dying?
zh: 是的，这很可怕，是的，感觉对面可能什么都没有，但还有什么别的选择呢，去紧紧抓住这个可能正在慢慢消亡的东西吗？ [[1041 ]那也不安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not safe either.
zh: 那也不安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: So leaning into change feels like to me the most important thing for folks to take away.
zh: 所以对我来说，拥抱变化是大家最应该记住的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think as part of that, I would just say grief is part of this and sometimes grief needs a funeral or do what you got to do to be sad.
zh: 我想作为其中的一部分，我只想说，悲伤是其中的一部分，有时候悲伤需要一场葬礼，或者做你需要做的事去难过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let your teams be sad.
zh: 让你的团队难过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let the people around you make space for that because with change comes shedding things that you loved and that sucks.
zh: 让你周围的人为此留出空间，因为变化意味着舍弃你所热爱的东西，这很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one of the other things that feels like it really came out, Lenny, is there is opportunity here and we got to start ignoring or muting or whatever some of this fear narrative because right now the data isn't saying there are no jobs for you.
zh: 我觉得另一件真正浮现出来的事情，Lenny，是这里有机会，我们必须开始无视或静音之类的这些恐惧叙事，因为现在数据并没有说没有工作留给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: The data is saying actually there's going to be a lot of opportunity created by this, particularly if you're willing to lean into reinvention, not what was the form of your job two years ago, but what might it be in five years?
zh: 数据实际上在说，这将创造大量的机会，尤其是如果你愿意拥抱重塑——不是你两年前的工作形态，而是五年后它可能是什么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: What else?
zh: 还有什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess breaking down walls is the other thing I was thinking, but what came to your list?
zh: 我猜打破壁垒是我想到的另一件事，但你清单上有什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, there's the minute kind of perspective of imagine your job isn't going to go away, imagine your job will continue, but be different.
zh: 嗯，有一种那种从分钟级别的角度来看的视角，想象你的工作不会消失，想象你的工作会继续存在，但会有所不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a real mind change for me when she said that because I was like, " Whoa.
zh: 当她说那句话时，对我来说真是一次思维上的转变，因为我当时的反应是，「哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, what is engineering going to look like in five years?"
zh: 是啊，五年后工程会是什么样子？」

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not going to go away.
zh: 它不会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be something different.
zh: 它会变成某种不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe there'll be more of it, like journalism.
zh: 也许会有更多的工程工作，就像新闻业一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's more journalists out there for better or for worse.
zh: 现在记者更多了，不管这是好事还是坏事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so far there's more PMs, more product, more engineers.
zh: 而且到目前为止，PM 更多了，产品更多了，工程师更多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So far that's going well.
zh: 到目前为止情况还不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another kind of takeaway is just be deliberate about what you give to AI.
zh: 另一个要点是，要有意识地去决定你把什么交给 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a few ways to think about it.
zh: 有几个角度可以去思考这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is just like what is AI going to do a terrible job at?
zh: 一个是，AI 会在什么事情上做得很糟糕？

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't do that.
zh: 那就别做那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it you love that you don't want it to take for you?
zh: 什么是你热爱的、不想让它替你拿走的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you avoid brain rot and just overrelying in AI?
zh: 你如何避免大脑腐化，避免过度依赖 AI？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a few things there, just AI is not going to... Don't give everything to AI.
zh: 有几点要注意，就是 AI 不会……不要把一切都交给 AI。

speaker: Molly Graham
en: Yeah. And I think also for a lot of us acknowledging that AI is not this super intelligent being, it is much more like an intern, and that means literally think about it as an intern. What would you give to an intern and what would you never give them?
zh: 是的。而且我认为对我们很多人来说，要承认 AI 并不是这个超级智能的存在，它更像一个实习生，这意味着真的要把它当成一个实习生来想。你会把什么交给实习生，又永远不会交给他们什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's the core of it.
zh: 我认为这就是事情的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like... Well, I feel like we said this, but there just may be some things we should never give away, and that is genuinely different.
zh: 而且我感觉……嗯，我感觉我们说过这个，但也许确实有些东西是我们永远不该交出去的，而这确实是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give away your Legos, but be discerning about what you should keep and what should be human and what humans are here for.
zh: 把你的乐高积木交出去，但要有辨别力地决定什么应该保留、什么应该是属于人类的、人类到底是为了什么而存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's part of the conversation for the next however many years is what are humans uniquely good at?
zh: 我认为在未来多少年里，对话的一部分就是：人类独特地擅长什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I think about there, just very concretely in my mind is be the person that guides what you're doing to a place, to the vision you have of the world you want, not just the simplest thing, not the thing that AI is kind of pointing to, just what do you actually want, and that's kind of our job for a while.
zh: 而我在这个问题上想的，很具体地在脑海里想的，就是成为那个引导你所做的事情走向某个方向的人，走向你想要的那个世界的愿景，而不只是最简单的东西，不只是 AI 大致指向的那个东西，而是你到底想要什么，而这在一段时间内就是我们的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the individual level, how can this new tool, this fun, intelligent intern that you've hired, let you do more of what you love, let you bring more joy into the world, let you lean into the things that you love doing.
zh: 在个人层面上，这个新工具，这个你雇来的有趣、聪明的实习生，怎么能让你做更多你热爱的事，让你给世界带来更多快乐，让你更投入于你喜欢做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can it amplify you instead of feeling like all you're doing is losing things to it?
zh: 它怎么能放大你，而不是让你感觉你所做的一切都在失去东西、失去给它？

speaker: Unknown
en: What a moment in time we're in, Molly, right now, trying to figure all this out.
zh: 我们正处在多么特别的一个时刻啊，Molly，就在此刻，试图把这一切搞清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to re-watch this in a year or two and make fun of ourselves.
zh: 一两年后我们会重新看这期节目，然后嘲笑自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, we're going to be, "We nailed it.
zh: 哦，我们会说，「我们搞定了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got everything right."
zh: 我们全都预测对了。」

speaker: Molly Graham
en: Perfect.
zh: 完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visionaries.
zh: 先知们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 哦，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, with that, Molly, is there anything else?
zh: 好了，说到这里，Molly，还有别的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you want to plug?
zh: 有什么想宣传的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you want to point people to?
zh: 有什么想让听众关注的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you want to tell people about that you're up to that might be interesting, useful to them?
zh: 有什么想告诉大家的、你正在做的、可能对他们有趣或有用的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll say two things.
zh: 我会说两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, I get a lot of wisdom, but also a lot of support for this kind of conversation from the community in Glue Club, and I think if you're a leader listening to this and feeling lonely and a little bit unsupported, find a community, whether it's Glue Club or another one, where you can talk about this because I do think leaning on each other to learn what's real and what's not and what's valuable and what it's not...
zh: 第一，我从 Glue Club 社区获得了大量的智慧，也有很多支持来做这类对话，我认为如果你是一位正在听这个节目、感到孤独和有点缺乏支持的领导者，找一个社区，不管是 Glue Club 还是别的社区，在那里你可以谈论这些，因为我确实认为相互依靠、去学习什么是真的、什么不是、什么有价值、什么没价值……

speaker: Unknown
en: So much of what we're doing in Glue Club is being like, "Is anybody else seeing this?"
zh: 我们在 Glue Club 做的很多事情就是问，「还有别人看到这个了吗？」

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is really valuable.
zh: 这真的很有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do it in Lennyland as well, but just get out there and talk about what's real and what's not.
zh: 你也可以在 Lennyland 里做到这一点，但就是要走出去，谈论什么是真的、什么不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't just stay in a sad, lonely hole.
zh: 不要只是待在一个悲伤、孤独的洞里。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the second thing I wanted to say, Lenny, is thank you for making space for this.
zh: 但我想说的第二件事，Lenny，是谢谢你为这个话题留出空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's important.
zh: 我认为这很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much space right now for the what should I do and what skills should I get and what course should I take and what tools should I try next?
zh: 现在有太多空间留给了那些问题：我该做什么、我该学什么技能、我该上什么课、我接下来该试什么工具？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who's hot today?
zh: 今天谁最火？

speaker: Unknown
en: But we aren't talking enough about the human side of this and what it feels like to be going through this for everyone.
zh: 但我们对这件事中人的这一面谈论得还不够,对每个正在经历这一切的人来说是什么感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm grateful that you reached out and we talked about making space to talk about this because I think hopefully people will leave feeling a little more sane and like, "Oh, everybody else is feeling a little crazy right now too."
zh: 所以我很感激你主动联系,我们谈了要留出空间来聊这个话题,因为我希望人们听完之后会感觉清醒一点,觉得“哦,原来其他人现在也有点觉得疯狂”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's lots of people out there grieving and that's okay.
zh: 现在外面有很多人在悲伤,这没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's normal.
zh: 这很正常。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you, Lenny.
zh: 谢谢你,Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, Molly.
zh: 谢谢你,Molly。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think of these...
zh: 我想到这些……

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a term for these sorts of episodes.
zh: 我给这类节目起了个说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I call them Trojan horse episodes where people come for all this tactical concrete, how do I use AI in this way, how do I become better PM, and then there's these like-
zh: 我叫它们特洛伊木马节目,人们是为了各种战术性的具体内容而来,比如我怎么在某个场景用 AI、怎么成为更好的 PM,然后还有这些——

speaker: Unknown
en: You get therapy.
zh: 你顺便接受了一次心理治疗。

speaker: Unknown
en: Important episodes that slip right in.
zh: 悄悄溜进来的重要节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, "Oh, okay.
zh: 然后你想,“哦,好吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't know I needed that, but that was very helpful."
zh: 我不知道自己需要这个,但确实很有帮助。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So welcome to the Trojan Horse.
zh: 欢迎来到特洛伊木马。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're smuggling in.
zh: 我们在偷偷走私进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love it.
zh: 我喜欢这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very timely with the Odyssey these days.
zh: 跟现在的《奥德赛》很应景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, dude.
zh: 是啊,老兄。
